## Coordinate move notes ({{FROM_PHASE}} = {{FROM_TAG}} -> {{TO_PHASE}} = {{TO_TAG}})

The move was scripted:

```bash
scripts/release-tools/measure-published-release.sh {{FROM_TAG}} \
  --predecessor-commit {{PREV_COMMIT}} >measurement.json
scripts/release-tools/advance-release-coordinate.sh {{FROM_TAG}} {{FROM_PHASE}} {{TO_TAG}} {{TO_PHASE}} \
  --measurements measurement.json
```

`measure-published-release.sh` read `{{FROM_TAG}}` without writing anything, and
`advance-release-coordinate.sh` applied every file listed in
`advance-release-coordinate-rules.pl`: the {{FROM_PHASE}} declaration (eleven pins)
and the {{TO_PHASE}} branch in `verify-public-key-lineage-coordinates.sh`, the
`{{TO_TAG}}) release_phase='{{TO_PHASE}}'` row, `{{TO_PHASE}}_{{FROM_PHASE}}_ANCESTOR_SHA` (`{{COMMIT}}`)
and its ancestor arm in `validate-source.sh`, `{{TO_PHASE}}` in every accumulating phase
list and frozen-policy message, the receipt row, the shipped phase table and
lineage matrix rows, the upgrade canary predecessor (`live {{FROM_VERSION}} {{TO_VERSION}}`),
the preflight predecessor default, the Homebrew `PRIOR_TAP_COMMIT` /
`PRIOR_CASK_BLOB` pins (`{{TAP_HEAD8}}` / `{{CASK_BLOB8}}`), and every test that pins the
current coordinate. History lines (the {{FROM_PHASE}} rows, burn records, incident
comments) are kept by explicit rules and did not move.

This move is based on `{{BASE}}`.

Read only, against the immutable release and the live tap:

| `checksums.txt` | `{{CHECKSUMS}}` |
| Darwin amd64 / arm64 archive | `{{DARWIN_AMD64}}` / `{{DARWIN_ARM64}}` |
| Linux amd64 / arm64 archive | `{{LINUX_AMD64}}` / `{{LINUX_ARM64}}` |
| Darwin amd64 / arm64 manifest | `{{MANIFEST_AMD64}}` / `{{MANIFEST_ARM64}}` |
| Evidence tag | `{{EVIDENCE_TAG}}`, object `{{EVIDENCE_OBJECT}}`, commit `{{EVIDENCE_COMMIT}}` |
| Homebrew tap head | `{{TAP_HEAD}}` "Publish signed Cask for {{FROM_TAG}}" (parent `{{TAP_PARENT8}}`) |
| Cask / Formula blob | `{{CASK_BLOB}}` / frozen `{{FORMULA_BLOB}}` |

The archives and `checksums.txt` were downloaded into a fresh `mktemp -d`
directory; they hash to the API digests, and the four archives hash to their
`checksums.txt` entries. The manifests are measured inside the darwin archives
(`adk-companion-manifest.json`), and each manifest's `artifact_digest` is the
`auto` binary beside it (amd64 `{{BINARY_AMD64_8}}`, arm64 `{{BINARY_ARM64_8}}`); both manifests
say version `{{FROM_VERSION}}` and build provenance `{{COMMIT12}}`. The tag header names
exactly `{{COMMIT12}}`, `commit`, and `{{FROM_TAG}}`, and the tag's SSH signature
verifies against the R2 trust root. The {{PREV_PHASE}} source `{{PREV_COMMIT8}}` is an ancestor
of `{{COMMIT12}}`, and `{{COMMIT12}}` is an ancestor of `main`. The tap head's parent is
the previous `PRIOR_TAP_COMMIT` (`{{TAP_PARENT8}}`), so the pin chain continues, the
Formula blob is frozen, and the Cask carries the four archive digests.

## Before `--apply`

| Item | Expected state |
|---|---|
| Ruleset `autopus-{{TO_TAG}}-release-authority` | **missing** until armed below |
| Deployment tag policy `{{TO_TAG}}` on `adk-companion-release` | **missing** until armed below |
| `{{TO_TAG}}` and `omp-context-evidence-{{TO_TAG}}` | absent on origin, and so is `omp-context-evidence-{{TO_TAG}}-source` |
| Draft release named `{{TO_TAG}}` | absent; Latest is `{{RELEASE_ID}}` (`{{FROM_TAG}}`) |

`verify-release-tag-ruleset.sh --armed` fails until both authorities exist.
Create them in the exact shape it accepts, then verify. Prep seals the ruleset
right after the tag exists. Never widen an older ruleset to cover the new tag.

```bash
gh api -X POST repos/autopus-ai/autopus-adk/rulesets --input - <<'JSON'
{"name":"autopus-{{TO_TAG}}-release-authority","target":"tag","enforcement":"active",
 "bypass_actors":[{"actor_id":204883817,"actor_type":"User","bypass_mode":"always"}],
 "conditions":{"ref_name":{"include":["refs/tags/{{TO_TAG}}"],"exclude":[]}},
 "rules":[{"type":"creation"},{"type":"update"},{"type":"deletion"}]}
JSON
gh api -X POST repos/autopus-ai/autopus-adk/environments/adk-companion-release/deployment-branch-policies \
  -f name={{TO_TAG}} -f type=tag
scripts/companion-release/verify-release-tag-ruleset.sh --armed
```

{{TO_PHASE}} needs fresh evidence. Never reuse any earlier report, attestation,
evidence commit, evidence tag object, draft, or workflow artifact. If
`scripts/release-tools/install-canary-helper.sh` changed since the helper was
installed, reinstall it in a real terminal before `--apply`.

```bash
export OMP_AUTH_BROKER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47311
export ADK_GATEWAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47312
export ADK_RELEASE_MODEL=gpt-6.1-sol
export ADK_RELEASE_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW=262144
scripts/release-tools/release-prep.sh --preflight
scripts/release-tools/release-prep.sh --apply
```

## Stop conditions

- `--apply` exit 75 leaves the prep lock retained on purpose. Inspect the
  remote state, fix only what is outside the source, and retry `--apply` on
  the identical source; never delete the lock or the evidence tag by hand.
- If the tap head moves off `{{TAP_HEAD8}}` before publication, re-measure
  (`measure-published-release.sh {{FROM_TAG}}`) and move the PRIOR pins first.
- The tag is immutable once pushed. If anything mismatches after that, do not
  move, delete, or reuse `{{TO_TAG}}`; carry the coordinate to `{{NEXT_TAG}}` and
  record the burn here.
- After publication, run the Upgrade Canary by hand
  (`gh workflow run upgrade-canary.yaml --ref {{TO_TAG}}`). A failure on the
  *previous* surface expectations is a canary fix, not a release fault.

## Next coordinate

After {{TO_TAG}} is published, the next move is
`measure-published-release.sh {{TO_TAG}} --predecessor-commit {{COMMIT}}` followed by
`advance-release-coordinate.sh {{TO_TAG}} {{TO_PHASE}} {{NEXT_TAG}} {{NEXT_PHASE}} --measurements …`. The script
refuses the move if a source file would pass 300 counted lines; the
coordinates file then needs older pin blocks carried to
`verify-public-key-lineage-shipped-pins.sh` first.
